quests.sentence: She sang and danced all night
quests.correctAnswer: She sang and danced all night.
quests.hint: Look for the subject of the sentence - is there really more than one, or is it doing two things at once?
quests.explanation: When one subject performs two actions joined by 'and,' no comma is needed before the conjunction.

quests.sentence: He grabbed his coat and rushed out the door
quests.correctAnswer: He grabbed his coat and rushed out the door.
quests.hint: Count how many different people are doing something in this sentence.
quests.explanation: Since 'he' performs both actions, this is one sentence with a compound predicate, not two joined sentences, so no comma is required.

quests.sentence: The dog barked and chased its tail
quests.correctAnswer: The dog barked and chased its tail.
quests.hint: A single subject doing two things in a row usually doesn't need a comma before 'and.'
quests.explanation: This sentence has only one subject performing two actions, so 'and' simply connects two verbs without needing a comma.

quests.sentence: The rain stopped and the sun came out
quests.correctAnswer: The rain stopped, and the sun came out.
quests.hint: Check whether each side of 'and' could stand alone as its own complete sentence.
quests.explanation: When 'and' joins two independent clauses that could each be their own sentence, a comma comes before the conjunction.

quests.sentence: I wanted to stay longer but my ride was leaving
quests.correctAnswer: I wanted to stay longer, but my ride was leaving.
quests.hint: Both halves of this sentence have their own subject and verb - that's a signal for a comma before 'but.'
quests.explanation: Two complete thoughts joined by 'but' are separated by a comma before the conjunction.

quests.sentence: She could take the bus or she could walk
quests.correctAnswer: She could take the bus, or she could walk.
quests.hint: Notice that each option could be its own full sentence on its own.
quests.explanation: When 'or' connects two independent clauses, a comma is placed before it, just as with 'and' and 'but.'

quests.sentence: He finished his homework and went to bed
quests.correctAnswer: He finished his homework and went to bed.
quests.hint: Ask yourself: is there one subject or two separate ones on each side of 'and'?
quests.explanation: 'He' does both actions, so this is a compound predicate with one subject, and no comma is needed.

quests.sentence: He finished his homework and his sister started hers
quests.correctAnswer: He finished his homework, and his sister started hers.
quests.hint: This time, look closely - does each half have its own separate subject?
quests.explanation: Because 'he' and 'his sister' are two different subjects with their own complete clauses, a comma comes before 'and.'

quests.sentence: We packed the car and drove to the coast
quests.correctAnswer: We packed the car and drove to the coast.
quests.hint: Compare this sentence to the one before it - how many different subjects are actually acting?
quests.explanation: Since 'we' is the only subject performing both actions, this is a compound predicate and needs no comma before 'and.'

quests.sentence: The store closed early it was a holiday
quests.correctAnswer: The store closed early. It was a holiday.
quests.hint: This is really two separate complete thoughts running together - where should one sentence end and the next begin?
quests.explanation: Two independent clauses with no connecting word need to be separated into two sentences with a period, rather than joined by only a comma.

quests.sentence: I called twice no one answered
quests.correctAnswer: I called twice. No one answered.
quests.hint: Try reading each half on its own - do they both work as complete sentences?
quests.explanation: When two complete thoughts have no joining word between them, they should be split into two sentences rather than run together.

quests.sentence: The movie was long we still enjoyed it
quests.correctAnswer: The movie was long, but we still enjoyed it.
quests.hint: This time, a joining word might work better than simply splitting the sentence in two.
quests.explanation: Adding the conjunction 'but' with a comma connects the two related ideas smoothly, instead of leaving them stuck together or split apart.

quests.sentence: My best friend from childhood moved to another city
quests.correctAnswer: My best friend from childhood moved to another city.
quests.hint: A long subject doesn't need to be cut off from its verb with a comma.
quests.explanation: Even a lengthy subject like 'my best friend from childhood' stays connected to its verb without a comma.

quests.sentence: Everyone who signed up for the trip should arrive early
quests.correctAnswer: Everyone who signed up for the trip should arrive early.
quests.hint: Resist the urge to add a comma just because the subject is long - check if it's really needed.
quests.explanation: A long subject followed directly by its verb does not need a comma between them, no matter how many words come before the verb.

quests.sentence: The tall man in the blue jacket waved at us
quests.correctAnswer: The tall man in the blue jacket waved at us.
quests.hint: Read the whole subject as one unit before deciding whether a comma belongs anywhere.
quests.explanation: Descriptive words attached directly to the subject, like 'in the blue jacket,' don't need to be set off with a comma.

quests.sentence: The trip was exciting exhausting and unforgettable
quests.correctAnswer: The trip was exciting, exhausting, and unforgettable.
quests.hint: This list describes qualities instead of naming objects, but the comma rule for lists doesn't change.
quests.explanation: A series of descriptive words is punctuated the same way as a series of nouns, with commas between each item.

quests.sentence: She wants to travel more save money and learn a language
quests.correctAnswer: She wants to travel more, save money, and learn a language.
quests.hint: Each item in this list is a short phrase, not a single word - the same comma pattern still applies.
quests.explanation: When a list contains phrases instead of single words, each phrase is still separated by a comma.

quests.sentence: He looked under the bed behind the couch and inside the closet
quests.correctAnswer: He looked under the bed, behind the couch, and inside the closet.
quests.hint: This list names three different places using short phrases - treat each one as a separate item.
quests.explanation: A series of prepositional phrases follows the same comma pattern as any other list.

quests.sentence: We cleaned the house and the guests started arriving
quests.correctAnswer: We cleaned the house, and the guests started arriving.
quests.hint: Check if each half of this sentence could stand alone before deciding on the comma.
quests.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'and' need a comma before the conjunction.

quests.sentence: I wanted to cook but we ordered pizza instead
quests.correctAnswer: I wanted to cook, but we ordered pizza instead.
quests.hint: Both sides of 'but' express a complete idea on their own.
quests.explanation: A comma comes before 'but' when it connects two independent clauses.

quests.sentence: The bakery sells bread pastries and cakes and it also caters events
quests.correctAnswer: The bakery sells bread, pastries, and cakes, and it also caters events.
quests.hint: This sentence has both a list of items and two joined independent clauses - handle each comma job separately.
quests.explanation: The three bakery items need list commas, and since 'it also caters events' is a separate independent clause, a comma precedes the second 'and' as well.

quests.sentence: The manager reviewed the file and approved the request
quests.correctAnswer: The manager reviewed the file and approved the request.
quests.hint: One person is doing two things here - check before adding any comma.
quests.explanation: This is a compound predicate with a single subject, so no comma belongs before 'and.'

quests.sentence: The manager reviewed the file and the assistant filed the paperwork
quests.correctAnswer: The manager reviewed the file, and the assistant filed the paperwork.
quests.hint: Compare the subjects on each side of 'and' carefully this time.
quests.explanation: Two different subjects each completing their own action means this is a compound sentence needing a comma before 'and.'

quests.sentence: Our neighbor with the loud motorcycle finally moved away
quests.correctAnswer: Our neighbor with the loud motorcycle finally moved away.
quests.hint: A descriptive phrase attached to the subject doesn't automatically call for a comma.
quests.explanation: The phrase 'with the loud motorcycle' describes the subject directly and doesn't need to be set off with a comma.

quests.sentence: The power went out the whole street went dark
quests.correctAnswer: The power went out, and the whole street went dark.
quests.hint: These two ideas are closely related - a joining word might connect them better than a full stop.
quests.explanation: Adding the conjunction 'and' with a comma links the cause and effect smoothly instead of leaving the clauses running together.

quests.sentence: The waiter forgot our order we had to ask twice
quests.correctAnswer: The waiter forgot our order. We had to ask twice.
quests.hint: These two complete thoughts don't need to be connected at all - they can simply stand as their own sentences.
quests.explanation: When two independent clauses aren't closely enough related to need a conjunction, splitting them into separate sentences with a period keeps the writing clear.

quests.sentence: The team practiced all week they still lost the match
quests.correctAnswer: The team practiced all week, but they still lost the match.
quests.hint: The outcome here contrasts with the effort described - a specific joining word can show that contrast.
quests.explanation: The conjunction 'but' with a comma shows the contrast between the two clauses more clearly than a period would.

quests.sentence: The new intern answered phones and organized files all week
quests.correctAnswer: The new intern answered phones and organized files all week.
quests.hint: One person, two tasks - decide if a comma is really needed before 'and.'
quests.explanation: Since the intern is the only subject completing both actions, this compound predicate needs no comma.

quests.sentence: The bus was late so several passengers missed their connections
quests.correctAnswer: The bus was late, so several passengers missed their connections.
quests.hint: Check whether each half of the sentence could work as its own complete sentence.
quests.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'so' need a comma before the conjunction.

quests.sentence: The recipe called for flour sugar butter and eggs but we were out of eggs
quests.correctAnswer: The recipe called for flour, sugar, butter, and eggs, but we were out of eggs.
quests.hint: This sentence combines a list with two joined independent clauses - punctuate each part on its own.
quests.explanation: The four listed ingredients need commas between them, and since 'we were out of eggs' is its own independent clause, a comma also comes before 'but.'
